common_name: Jamaican Me Crazy Daylily (Yellow with Dark Eggplant Halo)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun; this Trimmer introduction, registered in 1999, forms dependable clumps and blooms over a long midseason period.

directions: Plant in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun; Jamaican Me Crazy bears bright yellow flowers marked with a bold dark eggplant-purple halo above a green throat, creating a striking contrast. Registered by Trimmer in 1999, it has become a widely sold garden favorite valued for its clean color pattern and vigorous growth. Divide congested clumps in spring every few years to maintain bloom count.

common_name: Lacy Doily Daylily (Small Double Coral-Pink Rebloomer)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun; this compact Joiner introduction, registered in 1999, suits border edges and reblooms over summer with regular moisture.

directions: Plant in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun; Lacy Doily produces small double coral-pink flowers with a green center and golden-edged petals, held on compact scapes well suited to the front of a border. Registered by Joiner in 1999, it reblooms through summer and increases readily into a dense, floriferous clump. Divide every few years in spring to maintain vigor.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in average, well-drained soil in full sun; this dormant Durio introduction, registered in 1982, is a diploid spider-form type with extra-large, narrow-petaled blooms.

directions: Plant in average, well-drained soil in full sun; Spider Man bears bright red, extra-large spider-form flowers with narrow, recurved petals and a chartreuse throat, opening fresh each morning on tall scapes. Registered by Durio in 1982, this dormant diploid remains a favorite among growers of unusual-form daylilies for its dramatic size and color. Divide congested clumps in spring every few years to maintain vigor.

common_name: South Pacific Daylily (Coral Pink with Yellow Watermark)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun; this tetraploid cultivar, registered in 2005 from Belle Cook x Seabiscuit parentage, carries semi-evergreen foliage and reblooms with consistent moisture.

directions: Plant in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun; South Pacific bears coral-pink flowers with a bright yellow watermark and edge above a green throat, blooming in the early midseason with good rebloom. Registered in 2005 from Belle Cook x Seabiscuit parentage, this tetraploid carries semi-evergreen foliage and increases into dependable clumps. Divide every few years in spring to maintain bloom count.

common_name: Mardi Gras Parade Daylily (Rose-Lavender with Wine-Purple Eye)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun; this dormant Kroll introduction, registered in 1992, blooms in the early midseason on compact scapes.

directions: Plant in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun; Mardi Gras Parade bears ruffled rose-lavender flowers with a large wine-purple eyezone and chartreuse-green throat, blooming in the early midseason on compact two-foot scapes. Registered by Kroll in 1992, this dormant diploid has remained popular for its bold eye pattern and reliable clump formation. Divide congested clumps in spring every few years to maintain vigor.
